title: Portfolio
text:
A selection of some of my research and academic projects.


The Contexts That Bind Us: Networks, Multiplexity, and Embeddedness in Institutional Domains
Master’s Thesis · Leiden University & CBS (Statistics Netherlands) · 2026
How do our connections across family, work, education, and neighbourhoods relate to how much we trust other people? Using the CBS Person Network, a whole-population multilayer network covering approximately 17 million Dutch residents, I developed two individual-level measures of cross-domain embeddedness: multiplexity (whether the same people are connected across multiple domains) and participation evenness (how evenly ties are distributed across domains). A key methodological contribution was an adjusted multiplexity measure that accounts for administrative overlap between family and household registers. These measures were linked to the Social Cohesion and Well-being Survey (2020–2023, \(N\) = 28,483) to examine their association with generalised trust.
 Thesis ·  Conference Abstract



Immigration to Europe: An Interactive Dashboard
EMOS Presentation of Official Statistics · Leiden University · 2025
An interactive Shiny application that visualises immigration patterns across European countries using Eurostat data. The dashboard includes time-series views by country, choropleth maps of immigration counts, and maps showing immigration as a share of the national population. Data were sourced from the Eurostat migration (migr_imm8) and population (demo_pjan) databases, combined with NUTS-0 boundary files for spatial visualisation.
 Live app  Code



Housing Price Statistics in Den Bosch
European Master in Official Statistics (EMOS) – Statistical Production Systems · Statistics Netherlands (CBS) & Leiden University · 2025
This project implements a reproducible statistical production pipeline for computing average housing prices in Den Bosch. Using synthetic data from the Dutch buildings register and property sales records, the pipeline follows a five-stage workflow from raw data ingestion through preprocessing, validation, and statistical processing to final output. Each stage is modular and documented, reflecting the production system standards taught in the European Master in Official Statistics (EMOS) programme.
 Code



Social Factors Influencing Children’s Pro-Environmental Behaviour
Statistical Consulting Project · Leiden University · 2025
This study investigated how social factors influence pro-environmental behaviour (PEB) in children and adolescents aged 9 to 15 years. Participants (\(N\) = 164) from 13 classrooms across two schools completed an effort-based choice task across self, climate, and prosocial targets. We used generalized linear mixed-effects models to examine whether experimentally manipulated social norm messages affect effortful pro-environmental behaviour, and whether individual social susceptibility and classroom cohesion moderated these effects.

Research Experience

Master’s Thesis Intern — Statistics Netherlands (CBS), 2026

Processed linked administrative register data across five institutional domains (work, education, household, family, and neighbourhood) within the CBS microdata environment, covering approximately 17 million Dutch residents.
Developed an adjusted multiplexity measure to account for administrative overlap between family and household registers, and linked the population-scale multilayer network to survey data (\(N\) = 28,483) to investigate how the organisation of social ties across domains relates to generalised trust.
Built a reproducible R pipeline using data.table, arrow, and DuckDB for large-scale network computation.



Statistical Consulting Project — Leiden University, 2025-2026

Applied multilevel GLMMs to assess how peer norms shaped children’s pro-environmental effort choices in clustered classroom data (N = 164, 13 classrooms).
Developed a size-adjusted network density measure of classroom cohesion from peer-nomination data.



Research Project — Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, 2023

Contextualised and evaluated a brief self-report measure of well-being for workplace settings, examining its factor structure, reliability, and construct validity.



Research Project — Maastricht University, 2023

Designed and conducted a between-subjects experiment on mental-health stigma, including power analysis, ethical approval, and participant recruitment.
Exploratory analyses indicated lower stigma following a written narrative and lower anger following a video condition.

title: About me
text:
About me

  
    

    
  
    
     
  
  
    
     
  
  
    
     
  

  
  
Hi! I’m Milena, a quantitative researcher interested in how social environments shape individual outcomes and inequality. I work with population-scale administrative data and survey data, applying methods from psychometrics and measurement to multilevel modelling and social network analysis.
During my bachelor’s in Psychology at Maastricht University, I learned to think about behaviour in context. I also found a passion for the quantitative side of research, especially the challenge of measuring things that aren’t directly observable, like well-being or trust. A master’s in Statistics and Data Science at Leiden University gave me a strong foundation in statistical modelling, measurement, and working with complex data. For my master’s thesis at Statistics Netherlands (CBS), I worked with linked administrative registers covering approximately 17 million Dutch residents, investigating how people’s embeddedness across social domains such as work, neighbourhood, and household relates to their willingness to trust others. A discussion paper based on this work is currently in preparation.
I grew up in Brazil and moved to Belgium when I was eighteen. I spent two years working as an au pair caring for three young children, while studying Dutch at KU Leuven. Watching those children develop in a context quite different from my own made me curious about how much our surroundings shape who we become. I am currently based in Leiden.
In my free time, you will find me taking care of my lovely tropical plants, working in the garden, and having deep discussions about the meaning of life. I love learning about new cultures, reading about different perspectives, watching art house films, and going down rabbit holes about whatever has caught my attention lately. Whenever I get the chance, I also like to scuba dive.
